checks: Old saves retain pre-existing damage and gain healthy chassis/brake internals; every nested new field snapshots independently.
Actual wheel-bearing drag dissipates motion into its own heat and causes a local steering pull; stationary and missing bearings add no work.
Seized bearing locks the actual wheel without adding kinetic energy; force goes through the tyre and never into brake heat.
Bent tie rod changes trajectory; a broken rod ignores the rack; a seized rack holds its current steering position until replaced.
Collision and detachment damage local bearings, rods and ABS; targeted replacement, tuning, recovery and garage saves preserve unrelated faults.
Master-cylinder and booster failures reduce actual braking independently; failed ABS stops releasing pressure while leaving ordinary brakes working.
Disc heat boils degraded fluid and lengthens the pedal; cooling condenses vapour but leaves trapped air, which refill cannot fix.
Damage-off freezes permanent chassis/fluid wear; substeps conserve supplied bearing energy and overload affects only the loaded rotating corner.
All four bodies expose moving steering links and measured wheel camber; broken links separate and disposal removes the model.
Bearing rumble follows the damaged rotating wheel, stops with rotation or missing wheel, respects mechanical mix and emits finite PCM.
limits: Bounded fictional wheel-end, steering and dual-circuit approximations, no real-car calibration or vacuum/pipe/fluid CFD.
PCM checked numerically, not subjective listening; steering-link geometry checked, not physical hardware.
